section: Understanding the Tekton Results retention policy
job_statement: When managing pipeline results over time, I want to control how long results are retained in the database, so I can balance storage costs with audit and debugging requirements.
desired_outcomes: Minimize database storage costs
Ensure critical results are available when needed
Reduce time to configure retention rules
Prevent accidental deletion of important pipeline data
evidence: understanding-the-tekton-results-retention-policy-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Understanding the Tekton Results retention policy, lines 57-136. Assembly abstract states: 'The Retention Policy Agent manages how long the database retains Tekton Results and Records before pruning them.' Configuration via tekton-results-config-results-retention-policy config map. Fields include defaultRetention, policies, runAt for scheduling.
notes: Main job covering overall lifecycle management of pipeline results. Multiple user stories for different retention strategies (global default vs fine-grained rules).

section: Understanding the Tekton Results retention policy
job_statement: When I need simple retention management without complex rules, I want to set a global default retention period for all pipeline results, so I can ensure old results are automatically pruned without manual intervention.
parent_job: Control how long results are retained in the database
prerequisites: Understand retention period format (days or duration strings)
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to set up basic retention
Ensure consistent retention across all namespaces
Avoid manual cleanup of old results
evidence: understanding-the-tekton-results-retention-policy-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Understanding the Tekton Results retention policy, lines 124-126. Field 'defaultRetention' described as 'fallback retention period for Results and Records when no specific policy matches' with default value of '30d'.
notes: User story for simple global retention. Alternative to fine-grained policies for administrators who don't need namespace or label-based control.

job_statement: When different pipelines have different retention requirements, I want to define fine-grained retention policies based on namespaces, labels, annotations, or statuses, so I can retain critical results longer while pruning less important ones sooner.
parent_job: Control how long results are retained in the database
prerequisites: Know which namespaces, labels, or statuses to target
related_jobs: Label pipeline runs with criticality indicators
desired_outcomes: Minimize storage costs for non-critical results
Ensure compliance data is retained for required duration
Reduce complexity of retention configuration
Prevent accidental deletion of results under investigation
evidence: understanding-the-tekton-results-retention-policy-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Fine-grained retention policies (module op-fine-grained-retention-policies), lines 144-177. Describes 'policies' field with selectors for matchNamespaces, matchLabels, matchAnnotations, matchStatuses. First matching policy applies. Concrete example in lines 191-217 shows production failures retained 180 days, debug-annotated for 14 days, CI for 7 days.
notes: User story for advanced retention control. Enables differentiated retention based on multiple criteria. Evidence module is CONCEPT type from include graph.

job_statement: When critical pipeline failures occur in production, I want to retain those results for extended periods, so I can perform root cause analysis and meet compliance requirements without losing forensic data.
parent_job: Control how long results are retained in the database
desired_outcomes: Ensure failure data is available for investigation
Minimize risk of losing critical diagnostic information
Reduce time to identify root causes
Meet audit and compliance retention requirements
evidence: understanding-the-tekton-results-retention-policy-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Fine-grained retention policies, lines 191-200, 221. Example policy 'retain-critical-failures-long-term' matches production namespaces with criticality:high label and Failed status, retaining for 180 days. Line 221 confirms 'retains a failed Result in the production or prod-east namespace with the label criticality: high for 180 days'.
notes: Specific use case for production failure forensics. Persona is Platform engineer who investigates failures rather than Cluster admin who configures policies. Evidence module is CONCEPT type from include graph.

job_statement: When debugging complex pipeline issues, I want to mark specific results for extended retention using annotations, so I can preserve relevant data for ongoing investigations regardless of namespace or status.
parent_job: Control how long results are retained in the database
prerequisites: Have access to annotate pipeline runs
related_jobs: Share debugging data with support teams
desired_outcomes: Ensure results under investigation are not pruned
Minimize risk of losing debugging context
Reduce coordination overhead for retention decisions
Enable team members to preserve results independently
evidence: understanding-the-tekton-results-retention-policy-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Fine-grained retention policies, lines 201-206, 222. Example policy 'retain-annotated-for-debug' matches annotation 'debug/retain: true' with 14-day retention. Line 222 confirms 'retains any Result with the annotation debug/retain: true for 14 days'.
notes: Ad-hoc retention control via annotations. Enables developers/engineers to flag results for preservation without admin intervention to modify policies. Evidence module is CONCEPT type from include graph.

section: Understanding the Tekton Results retention policy
job_statement: When I need automated database cleanup, I want to schedule the pruning job using cron syntax, so I can control when old results are deleted and avoid impacting production workloads.
parent_job: Control how long results are retained in the database
prerequisites: Know cluster usage patterns to avoid peak times
desired_outcomes: Minimize performance impact during business hours
Ensure pruning runs at predictable intervals
Reduce manual intervention for cleanup
Avoid storage exhaustion from missed pruning
evidence: understanding-the-tekton-results-retention-policy-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Understanding the Tekton Results retention policy, lines 120-122. Field 'runAt' described as 'when the pruning job runs' using cron schedule format with default '7 7 * * 7' (every Sunday at 7:07 a.m.). Example at line 109 shows custom schedule '*/1 * * * *' (every minute for testing). Production example at line 188 shows '0 2 * * *' (daily at 2 a.m.).
notes: Scheduling aspect of retention management. Decouples policy definition from execution timing. Important for managing database load and avoiding disruption.

job_statement: When managing CI/CD pipelines with different lifecycle requirements, I want to apply shorter retention periods to ephemeral CI results while keeping production results longer, so I can optimize storage costs without losing important operational data.
parent_job: Control how long results are retained in the database
prerequisites: Separate CI and production workloads by namespace
Define appropriate retention periods for each environment
desired_outcomes: Minimize storage costs for temporary CI results
Ensure production results meet operational requirements
Reduce time to implement environment-specific policies
Avoid storage waste from long-lived test results
evidence: understanding-the-tekton-results-retention-policy-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Fine-grained retention policies, lines 212-217, 224-225. Example policy 'short-term-ci-retention' matches namespace 'ci' with 7-day retention (line 216), versus 'default-production-policy' matching 'production'/'prod-east' namespaces with 60-day retention (lines 206-211). Lines 224-225 confirm differential retention: '7 days' for CI vs '60 days' for production.
notes: Environment-based retention strategy. Common pattern for optimizing costs while meeting different compliance/operational needs per environment. Evidence module is CONCEPT type from include graph.

section: Understanding the Tekton Results retention policy
job_statement: When configuring retention policies in TektonConfig, I want to understand the precedence and evaluation order of policies, so I can design effective rules without unintended overlaps or conflicts.
parent_job: Control how long results are retained in the database
prerequisites: Know which results need special retention
desired_outcomes: Minimize configuration errors from policy conflicts
Ensure most specific policies take precedence
Reduce time to troubleshoot retention issues
Avoid unexpected deletions from policy misunderstandings
evidence: understanding-the-tekton-results-retention-policy-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Fine-grained retention policies, lines 148-149, 160. Line 148 states 'Tekton Results evaluates the policies in order, and applies the first matching policy'. Line 160 clarifies 'All selector types use AND logic, meaning a Result must satisfy all specified conditions to match'. Example at lines 191-217 shows ordered policies with increasingly specific selectors at the top.
notes: Understanding policy evaluation is prerequisite to effective configuration. First-match ordering means policy order matters. AND logic for selectors requires understanding all criteria must be met. Evidence module is CONCEPT type from include graph.
